transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-02-12 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Noah (CSM), Marcus (Orchid procurement), Sana (Orchid legal), Ethan (Orchid platform), Diane (Orchid security)

Summary:
Priya opened with commercial readout and reminded stakeholders this is to align pricing, SLA expectations and next steps for an onboarding pilot. Main themes: committed usage options vs variable billing, SLA windows (p95/P99), data residency/KMS, DPA redlines and a small technical test for VPC peering and KMS flow.

Topics:
1) Pricing workbook walkthrough
2) SLA targets and penalties
3) DPA/MSA redlines and audit logs
4) Technical onramp: VPC peering, KMS, private deployment options
5) Next steps and timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya: okay hi everybody thanks for joining, we know everyone's busy so we'll keep this focused, um the goal is to lock the commercial path and align legal and ops so we can kick the pilot next week
[00:18] Marcus: yeah thanks priya, appreciate it, we just want clarity on the price floor and what triggers additional approvals in finance, the last call left a bit of ambiguity on committed vs burst capacity
[00:29] Priya: totally, so quick recap we gave two pricing tracks, self-serve hosted with variable usage and a dedicated reserved pool with monthly commitment, the workbook i'll send has breakouts for token tiers, embedding units and egress fees
[00:45] Ethan: quick Q, how are egress fees defined? are they per-request or per-GB? sometimes vendor sheets say per-GB but the example looked per-request when we modeled it
[00:58] Liam: good call, sorry there's a mix in the example, actual egress is per-GB out of region plus a small per-request overhead for tiny payloads, we'll tidy that in the workbook, that's my bad, auto-export formatting glitch i think
[01:16] Sana: on DPA/MSA, we have standard redlines for data at rest encryption, KMS control, and access to logs — especially audit logs for model inputs, we can't allow vendor side keys without escrow options or a bring-your-own-key model
[01:34] Noah: just to add, Redwood private supports BYOK with KMS/HSM integration and we have enterprise docs, but there is an ops path if you need us to manage keys under an SLA, it's configurable
[01:49] Diane: are those logs kept on Redwood console only? we need syslog forward to our SIEM and retention of 1 year for auditability
[02:04] Liam: yes we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding, retention is configurable from 30 days up to 1 year on paid plan, we should capture the retention needs in the DPA appendix
[02:21] Marcus: on SLA, finance wants to understand credits and remedies; your SLA doc mentions latency SLOs and uptime tiers but not the credit math for p95 violation, can you summarize?
[02:38] Priya: quick version, hosted plan has best-effort with no uptime credits, dedicated/reserved pool includes 99.95% monthly uptime target with credits scaling by severity, p95 latency guarantee is 200ms for small gen tokens on dedicated NVMe-backed instances, p99 is 500ms — credits flow if we miss monthly windows, detailed formula in the SLA appendix
[02:58] Sana: that p95 figure seems optimistic, given our peak bursts and long context prompts — also we require a minimum telecom SLA with penalty cap that finance will accept, what's the cap?
[03:16] Liam: caps depend on commitment tier; typically we set an upper credit cap of 30% of monthly committed fees for severe outages, but we can discuss a different cap for enterprise tier in negotiations
[03:33] Ethan: how does fallback work if dedicated capacity is exhausted? do you route to hosted and what are the data implications? we have strict PII handling rules
[03:46] Priya: good question — our smart routing can fallback to a compatible model in hosted but only under configured policy; for customers with strict data residency we can disable fallback or ensure fallback uses a private variant that preserves KMS keys, but that may impact latency/cost
[04:05] Marcus: finance also asked about a minimum usage commitment term — is it 3 months or 12 months? and what's the discount curve?
[04:16] Priya: standard is quarterly for pilot (3 months) with 12-month options for better discounts, workbook will show 5/10/15% discount bands depending on committed token volume, and there's an early-exit pro-rata formula
[04:30] Sana: about DPA redlines — we need explicit language about deletion of data in transit and at rest, and an ability to demonstrate deletion on request for specific customer datasets
[04:44] Liam: we have a data lifecycle API that can remove cached prefixes and invalidate KV cache instances for a customer; for full deletion traceability we can emit attestations but for deep archival cleans there is a 48–72 hour backend window depending on replication — we'll document that
[05:02] Diane: can Redwood run on-prem for air-gap, we have a regulated environment where no external egress is allowed, what are the private on-prem constraints?
[05:15] Noah: yes we have a Redwood Private package for air-gapped installs, it's heavier lift — requires dedicated infra, but you get local control plane and full KMS integration; onboarding timeline is typically 6–8 weeks for initial deploy plus validation testing
[05:33] Marcus: timeline matters — procurement wants a go/no-go by end of month, so we need price and legal terms by 2026-02-18, is that possible?
[05:45] Priya: yes we'll aim for that, i'll send the updated workbook tonight and liam will push the SLA appendix and benchmark deck mid-week
[05:57] [00:06:00] Liam: switching to technical runbook, if you do Dedicated we'll provision a reserved GPU pool, we support batching and KV cache tuning to hit your latency targets, for the pilot we recommend a 2-GPU pool with NVMe backed model cache
[06:20] Ethan: can you show a sample config? specifically how batching interacts with low-latency interactive queries versus high-throughput embeddings?
[06:32] Liam: yep, the sample config shows two routes: interactive route with aggressive min-batch=1 and max-latency 80ms, and batch route for embeddings with batching window 250ms, that way we isolate tail latency
[06:47] Ethan: and what's the expected cost delta for the two routes? i.e. if 60% interactive and 40% batch, how does that map to committed tokens?
[06:59] Priya: we'll model that in the workbook — rough rule of thumb: interactive higher unit cost due to lower batching efficiency, embedding batch route more cost-efficient by ~30-40% on token unit basis
[07:14] Marcus: legal aside, we may need a DPA appendix that includes SOC2 attestation and a certificate copy, do you have a current SOC2 report?
[07:25] Noah: yes current SOC2 Type II report available and we can share via NDA link; we also offer ISO request package on enterprise tier
[07:36] Sana: about indemnity and liability, we need to cap model output risk, especially for regulated responses, do you have a model governance clause?
[07:49] Priya: we include a model governance schedule that documents content policies and an optional monitoring add-on, however most model hallucination liability is a negotiation point — we often agree a mutual indemnification for breaches of data protection obligations
[08:03] Diane: security control question: can we enforce RBAC and SCIM provisioning from our IdP? we use AzureAD SAML and SCIM for user lifecycle
[08:15] Liam: yes SSO via SAML and SCIM user provisioning supported, plus fine-grained RBAC; we'll need an admin integration step during onboarding
[08:27] Marcus: ok lets talk pricing tweaks — finance flagged potential data-transfer fees for cross-region usage, can those be capped? we have multi-region customers and transfer unpredictability concerns
[08:40] Priya: we can add a cross-region egress cap as a negotiated term or include a blended egress rate in the committed contract to simplify forecasting, that's doable for enterprise customers
[08:54] [00:09:00] Sana: small nit: DPA needs clause for subprocessor list and change notification window, we need to know if Redwood adds additional subprocessors mid-contract
[09:05] Noah: we publish a subprocessors list and give 30 days notice for changes, can do 45 days if required by policy, we'll add that to the DPA appendix
[09:17] Ethan: technical test — for VPC peering we need a dry-run for connectivity and a small inference workload, how long does that take to provision?
[09:29] Liam: VPC peering test can be provisioned in a day once network ACLs are set and keys exchanged, the inference test itself we can run for an hour to capture latency/throughput numbers, we recommend running 3 x 1-hour windows across different times of day for representative samples
[09:46] Marcus: fine, schedule it, procurement wants us to see real numbers before committing, also want a slide that maps potential credit exposure to outage scenarios for finance
[10:00] Priya: we'll produce a short risk-credit mapping slide and include it in the SLA appendix
[10:12] [00:10:00] Sana: DPA redlines — we want 7 year retention allowances for audit records but data deletion guarantees for training inputs, can you reconcile that?
[10:24] Liam: yes retention for audit logs is different from training retention, we can keep audit logs for extended windows but training data retention will be minimized and we will not use customer-specific inputs for weight updates unless explicitly opted-in, that will be spelled out in the DPA training clause
[10:41] Diane: one more on keys, we need attestation that BYOK keys are never exported and HSM logs are accessible, is a technical run on HSM possible as part of pilot?
[10:52] Noah: we can include a technical attestation and sample HSM audit log extract (redacted) for the legal review, real HSM log access needs scoped controls but doable under an audit engagement
[11:07] Marcus: circling back to pricing, what's the onboarding fee for Private vs Dedicated? we have budget constraints for initial PoC
[11:19] Priya: onboarding fee for Dedicated reserved is usually a one-time setup fee $25k for initial capacity and integrations, Private on-prem has a larger professional services fee starting at $125k due to infra and install work, but we can reduce initial price for pilot if you commit to conversion
[11:36] Ethan: is there a sandbox / eval account with limited tokens to run functional tests without consuming committed usage?
[11:46] Liam: yes we provide a sandbox with limited quota, not tied to billing, useful for functional tests and basic integration — the performance won't mirror dedicated NVMe though
[11:58] [00:20:00] Priya: ok let's recap milestones: 1) Priya sends updated pricing workbook and commitment bands 2) Liam shares benchmark deck and Dedicated sample config 3) schedule VPC peering dry-run 4) Sana to provide DPA redlines by 2026-02-18 5) finance wants credit mapping slide — we'll deliver mid-week
[12:23] Marcus: that aligns, one small ask: can you include a pathway for sandbox -> dedicated conversion with no IP changes to our workloads? switching infra often causes rework
[12:35] Liam: yes we support a lift-and-shift approach with consistent endpoints and client creds, conversion is typically a config flip plus data sync for KV caches, we document client compatibility in the runbook
[12:49] Sana: we'll also include a legal gating item: acceptance criteria for pilot, we need defined success metrics otherwise procurement will withhold sign-off, typical metrics are P95 under X ms, error rate below Y% and cost per 1k tokens below $Z
[13:06] Priya: good point — we'll propose success metric slate: p95 <= 250ms interactive, error rate <0.5%, and cost within agreed band; acceptance is sign-off by both teams after three test windows
[13:22] Ethan: question about billing granularity — do you bill per-token, per-request, or blended SKU? we want predictable monthly invoices for finance
[13:33] Priya: billing supports per-token and blended SKUs for enterprise customers, we can do a flat monthly commit + overage charge to simplify invoicing
[13:45] Marcus: can finance get a sample invoice? they want to see line items and how credits appear
[13:54] Noah: yes we'll include a sample invoice and a credits example in the workbook
[14:08] [00:30:00] Priya: ok any final blockers or unresolved items for today?
[14:15] Sana: DPA redlines and subprocessors notice period to be confirmed, also we need to validate the model governance clause about not using our customer data to train public models
[14:27] Priya: understood, we'll include explicit carve-outs for training in the DPA schedule, liam will provide the technical attestation for data non-use
[14:36] Marcus: procurement to evaluate the blended egress cap option versus standard rates; we'll pick one in the week
[14:44] Ethan: i'll assemble traffic profile and sample prompts and send to liam for the pilot config
[14:52] Priya: perfect, we'll aim to have everything consolidated by 2026-02-18 so you can queue legal and finance reviews
[15:02] [00:40:00] Closing notes:
- Links shared: pricing workbook (link placeholder: https://redwood.app/drive/pricing-orchid-2026), SLA appendix draft (https://redwood.app/drive/sla-draft), Sandbox runbook (https://redwood.app/drive/sandbox-runbook).
- Follow-up meeting proposed: 2026-02-19 11:00 PST for legal readout and pilot scheduling.

Crosstalk and imperfect transcriptions noted: occasional speaker labels may be off, small words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KMS/KMSH, NVMe/NVM-E spelled), product names sometimes shortened (Redwood Private => R.Private).
